name: Pumpkin
intro: A pumpkin is a big, round fruit. It grows on a long vine.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: Most pumpkins are bright orange.
Some pumpkins are white, green, or yellow.
Most pumpkins are round.
A pumpkin has a thick, hard shell.
Inside, it has soft pulp and lots of seeds.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Pumpkins first grew in Mexico and the southern United States.
Now people grow them all over the world.
Only Antarctica is too cold for pumpkins.
Many pumpkins grow on farms and in gardens.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A pumpkin plant needs lots of sun.
It needs warm soil to start growing.
It needs water to keep the soil damp.
It likes rich soil that drains well.
It needs lots of room for its long vines.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A pumpkin starts as a small seed.
The seed grows into a plant with long vines.
The plant grows male and female flowers.
Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
Then a pumpkin grows until its skin is hard.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A pumpkin is really a fruit because it has seeds.
Pumpkins are mostly water.
People carve pumpkins into jack-o'-lanterns for Halloween.
You can roast pumpkin seeds for a snack.
Giant pumpkins can be as heavy as a small car.

vocab.meaning: A long stem that creeps along the ground.
A small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
Yellow dust that flowers need to make fruit.
A pumpkin with a face carved into it.
